description: Profit target after a range/triangle breakout: exit when price has travelled the height of the pattern (captured at the breakout) beyond the breakout level.
pseudocode: target = breakoutLevel + heightMultiple * (rangeHigh - rangeLow); ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && high[0] >= target
book_order_type: limit order at the measured move target

complexity.reason: the pattern height and breakout level must be captured at entry and held as state; no pivot projection is needed for the horizontal-range special case

chapter_title: Part II: Trend Lines and Channels (introduction)

name: WedgeBySlopeComparison
quote: When a channel has a wedge shape, it is due to urgency. For example, in a wedge top, the slope of the trend line is greater than the slope of the trend channel line.
description: A rising channel is a wedge (favoring a reversal read) when the trend line's slope exceeds the trend channel line's slope by more than wedgeSlopeMultiple, provided at least two pushes have formed ('what first distinguishes a wedge from a channel is the second pullback').
pseudocode: slope(trendLine) > slope(channelLine) * wedgeSlopeMultiple && pushCount >= 2
book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: needs both projected lines' slopes plus a minimum push count

chapter_title: Trend Channel Lines

name: TwoLegPullbackAfterWedgeReversal
quote: Traders will see the turn down from the wedge top and most will wait for at least two legs down before they look for the next major pattern to buy or sell.
description: After a wedge-top reversal (T14-08 fading), require at least a two-legged pullback (two separate down-legs with an intervening bounce) before treating the correction as complete for the next setup.
pseudocode: legCountSinceWedgeTop >= minLegs
book_order_type: n/a (context)

complexity.reason: 'leg' is not yet defined at the bar level in this chapter; leg counting is fully developed in Chapter 20 and needed here as a prerequisite

chapter_title: Trend Channel Lines

name: FinalFlagSlopePredictsNewTrendSlope
quote: One final minor observation is that the slope of the final flag of a trend often provides an approximation of the slope of the new trend.
description: The slope of the trend/channel line through a trend's final flag can be used as an initial estimate of the slope of the new, opposite-direction trend after a reversal.
pseudocode: newTrendSlopeEstimate = -slope(finalFlagTrendLine)
book_order_type: n/a (context estimate, not a trade trigger)

complexity.reason: requires identifying the 'final flag' -- a pattern-recognition judgment call (book 3 territory) -- before its slope means anything, and Brooks himself calls it 'of limited value'

chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Trend

name: WedgeOvershootReversalEntry
quote: The easiest reversal setup to spot is a three-push pattern in a channel with a wedge shape, where the third push overshoots the trend channel line and reverses with a strong reversal bar
description: Entry (countertrend, long side mirrored): three pushes down in a bear channel, the third overshooting the bear trend-channel line, followed by a strong bull reversal bar; buy at the next open. Prefer the second entry (T21-28).
pseudocode: threePushesDown && low[1] < bearChannelLine.at(1) && bullReversalBar[0] && close[0] > low[1]
book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the reversal bar high

complexity.reason: wedge/three-push detection with channel-line overshoot

notes: Reversal-bar test as in TP4-09.
chapter_title: Spike and Channel Trend

name: WedgeCorrectionMinimumBarCount
quote: After a large wedge bottom, the market usually has at least a two-legged rally that tests the top of the wedge...and the number of bars in the correction is usually at least a third or so of the number of bars in the wedge.
description: Filter/context: after a wedge-bottom reversal, treat the correction as still incomplete (likely to need a further, larger leg, and a full reversal reading as premature) until the rally's bar count reaches a fraction of the wedge's own bar count.
pseudocode: wedgeBottomDetected && correctionBarsSoFar < minCorrectionFraction * wedgeBarCount
book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: requires wedge detection (three-push, swing pivots) plus a bar-count ratio test

chapter_title: Reversal Day

name: MiddayThreePushCountertrendLikelyFails
quote: Sometimes there are three countertrend lazy pushes, creating a wedge flag. At other times the third leg fails to surpass the second, and this forms a head and shoulders flag (most head and shoulders reversal patterns fail and become continuation patterns).
description: Filter: during the midday range following a morning trend leg, a developing three-push countertrend pattern (wedge or head-and-shoulders shaped) is more likely to fail and resume the original trend than to become a genuine reversal; bias against fading the morning trend on this pattern and prefer resuming with-trend entries once it fails.
pseudocode: morningLegDirection != 0 && threeCountertrendPushesDetected(sinceMorningLeg) -> biasWithTrend = morningLegDirection
book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot / three-push detection restricted to the midday window
